title: Joey Jordison - Wikipedia
notes: Read to character 100,000 of 103,722. Nathan Jonas Jordison, born 26 April 1975, Des Moines, Iowa; died in his sleep 26 July 2021, Waukee, Iowa, aged 46, no cause announced. Played guitar before a first kit from his parents at eight; self-taught, then lessons with a teacher of R&B and jazz technique; Modifidious (speed/thrash metal). Slipknot 1995 to December 2013 as #1, the first four studio albums, produced 9.0: Live (2005). Murderdolls (drums and rhythm guitar; revived the Rejects as Murderdolls in 2002, reunited 2010). Scar the Martyr 2013 to 2016; Vimic (Open Your Omen, recorded about 2014, released 2025); Sinsaenum from 2016. Filled in for Metallica at Download 2004 (8 of 13 songs), Satyricon (US tour, late 2004), Ministry (MasterBaTour 2006), Korn (2007), Rob Zombie (after 2010). Influences named: Neil Peart, Keith Moon, John Bonham, Peter Criss, Gene Krupa, Buddy Rich; also Lars Ulrich, Charlie Benante, Vinnie Paul, Dave Lombardo; admired Dale Crover. 'Technical parts influenced by thrash metal, with blast beats and fills at high tempos'. Pearl drums and hardware, Paiste cymbals, Remo heads, Promark sticks, ddrum triggers, Roland electronics. Rhythm readers' poll (August 2010): best drummer of the previous 25 years ('I'm at a loss for words'); Loudwire readers (2013): greatest metal drummer; Metal Hammer Golden Gods (2016). Acute transverse myelitis revealed 2016, symptoms from 2010, lost the use of his left leg at the end of his Slipknot years. Slipknot announced on 12 December 2013 that he had left; he said he had been fired.

title: Slipknot (band) - Wikipedia
notes: Read to character 100,000 of 214,919. Crahan, Colsefni and Gray started the Pale Ones in September 1995; Gray invited Jordison to a rehearsal and he joined as drummer, moving Crahan to percussion; he brought in Josh Brainard; first show as Meld on 5 November 1995; he suggested the name Slipknot, after one of their songs, in late-night sessions at the gas station where he worked nights. Members wear masks and matching jumpsuits and were numbered 0 to 8; masks updated with each album, custom-made by Screaming Mad George since 2000; 'hydraulic drum risers' among the stage sets. Left 12 December 2013; Jay Weinberg replaced him; Eloy Casagrande replaced Weinberg in 2024.

title: Slipknot (album) - Wikipedia
notes: Released 29 June 1999 (Roadrunner); produced by Ross Robinson and Slipknot at Indigo Ranch, Malibu, 29 September to 11 November 1998 and February 1999. Jordison (#1) co-mixed it with Robinson; credited with music on Wait and Bleed and Surfacing; said the band's roots were 'death metal, thrash metal, speed metal'. Wait and Bleed Grammy-nominated (Best Metal Performance, 2001).

title: Iowa (album) - Wikipedia
notes: Released 28 August 2001; recorded 22 January to 16 March 2001 at Sound City and Sound Image, Van Nuys; produced by Ross Robinson and Slipknot, mixed by Andy Wallace. Jordison and Paul Gray began writing in October 2000 and wrote most of it. 'Blast beat percussion', one of the few mainstream albums with it; a review: 'an abrasive amalgam of death metal blastbeats and bestial grunting'. Jordison: 'the album we really wanted to make'. He designed the Slipknot and tribal-S logos. The 2011 reissue carries the Disasterpieces audio (London Arena, 2002).

title: Vol. 3: (The Subliminal Verses) - Wikipedia
notes: Released 25 May 2004; recorded July 2003 to January 2004 at The Mansion, Laurel Canyon, with Rick Rubin (his only Slipknot album); Jordison credited with drums and mixing. Singles Duality, Vermilion, Before I Forget (Grammy, Best Metal Performance, 2006), The Blister Exists. Jordison: 'almost as if Slayer was tapping on Radiohead'.

title: All Hope Is Gone - Wikipedia
notes: Released 26 August 2008; produced by Dave Fortman and Slipknot at Sound Farm, Jamaica, Iowa, February to June 2008. Jordison and Jim Root wrote Sulfur together in an evening; he called it 'the record that I've wanted Slipknot to sound like'. Psychosocial Grammy-nominated (Best Metal Performance). A broken ankle cancelled European dates.

title: Disasterpieces - Wikipedia
notes: Filmed 16 February 2002 at the London Docklands Arena, one of the last European dates of the Iowa tour; directed by Matthew Amos; released November 2002; shot with 26 cameras, mask cameras on most members (Jordison's camera was not on his mask). 'Joey Drum Solo' is disc one, track 14. 4x platinum in the US.

title: Matt Stocks, 'The 10 drummers that inspired Joey Jordison', Metal Hammer (2016 interview; Louder, 28 April 2023)
notes: His ten: Bonham ('I have to start with John Bonham'; Led Zeppelin II; his uncle played him Bonham's solos), Neil Peart (2112, 'I still can't play like Neil Peart!'), Keith Moon (Quadrophenia; 'one of the most eccentric, fast and crazy drummers of all time'), Bill Ward ('the best heavy metal drummer of all time ... the ultimate groove and swing'), Lars Ulrich ('his double bass was completely on point'; filling in at Download), Charlie Benante ('I busted my ass trying to learn the double bass parts to A Skeleton in the Closet'; 'hugely responsible for training me'), Brann Dailor ('one of my best friends ... counterparts'), Danny Heifetz (Mr. Bungle, 'switches from jazz into metal'), Hellhammer ('his double bass and blasts and fills'), Dave Lombardo ('the fucking master'; Reign in Blood in his Easter basket in 1986; 'my ultimate influence as far as this type of music goes'; Fantômas at the Troubadour, 1998). First records: Tattoo You, Quadrophenia, Led Zeppelin I to IV, In Through the Out Door.

title: Lars-Oliver Horl, 'Interview und Gear-Chat: Joey Jordison', bonedo.de, 2 December 2017
notes: In German; Hamburg, Vimic promotion. Learned by playing along to his favourite records; years in a school drum corps taught him stick control ('Dort habe ich viel über Stick Control gelernt'); speed and double bass take persistence, past a threshold; practises three to four hours a day off tour. Upside-down drumming with Slipknot: adrenaline and fear; a loose harness nearly let him slip, the tighter one made breathing hard. Influences: Moon, Peter Criss, Bonham, Bill Ward, Charlie Watts; Lars Ulrich, Lombardo, Benante, Pete Sandoval, Tomas Haake, Danny Carey, Dale Crover (the Melvins his favourite band); Stewart Copeland the reason for his octobans. Records recommended: Quadrophenia, Billy Cobham's Spectrum, Fantômas, Morbid Angel's Blessed Are the Sick. 2017 kit: Pearl Reference, piano black, two 22x18 bass drums, toms 8x8, 10x8, 12x8, 13x9, floor 16x16, snare 14x6.5 Masters Maple (Roland trigger, in a caption); Demon Drive double pedal on the right bass drum only; Paiste RUDE Wild hats and chinas, Signature Power crashes and ride, Signature splashes; Promark TX515W; four octobans and Roland pads not on that tour.

title: 'Joey Jordison: die besten Grooves und Fills des Slipknot-Drummers' (Drum Play-Alike 8), bonedo.de, 8 September 2025
notes: In German, with notation. People = Shit: a traditional blast beat at 210, a double-bass passage at 220, then the 'Hammer-Blast' (kick, snare and china together in continuous sixteenths) and a one-bar 32nd fill around the kit; the chorus a half-time beat with the kick on the last sixteenth, two kicks with the snare on 2 and 4; the chorus ends on a sextuplet snare roll with china accents. Duality's verse leaves out the backbeat, kick and hat on the off-beats. Psychosocial: the intro's sextuplet four-hands-two-feet fill. Before I Forget: a mosh part with groupings of three.

title: Samantha Landa, '5 Things Every Drummer Can Learn From Joey Jordison', Drumeo Beat (updated 22 August 2022)
notes: Self-taught, then an R&B and jazz teacher; brought death-metal double bass into the mainstream after Metallica and Slayer; Jordison (via a Drum! magazine interview): 'Double bass needs to be used as a dynamic, not for flash'; 'Songs are not drum solos'; 'Never be scared to venture out and learn to adapt to different styles of music'. Eyeless opens on a drum-and-bass-like figure; Purity's verse on a snare roll. Stewart Copeland: 'All that cool shit that he does with both his feet and his hands has to be marveled at.'

title: 'Slipknot's Jay Weinberg: Copying Joey Jordison Would Be Insulting', Loudwire, 13 April 2016 (from MusicRadar)
notes: Weinberg: 'Joey's one of the greatest drummers we've ever had the privilege of witnessing'; 'Why would I want to be Joey Jordison, why would I try to mimic what he's done?'
